Que proposent réellement les principaux: What are the main political parties in the race really proposing on immigration? La Converse breaks it down.
Avec des plateformes électorales dévoilé: With party platforms released only days before the federal vote, it’s hard to see clearly. They’re also far from easy to decode. So we decided to sum up the main parties’ proposals on three issues: immigration, Indigenous rights and systemic racism. Since I’ve often covered this topic, I chose to look at immigration.
Ce sujet a été choisi en raison de sa pl: This topic was chosen because of its growing place in Canadian public debate. The goal is to give readers a clear, factual overview of the various election promises so they can make an informed vote. So I went through each party’s plan, dozens of pages each, with a fine-tooth comb.
I hope this helps clear things up.
<strong>Demandeurs d’asile, travailleurs: Asylum seekers, temporary workers, international students, permanent residents… These are words that have come up regularly throughout this federal election campaign, the outcome of which we’ll know on Monday, April 28. But what are the main political parties in the race really proposing on immigration? La Converse breaks it down.
Face à la crise du logement, de la santé: Faced with the housing and health care crises, as well as the inflation Canadians are experiencing, immigration is being singled out in this <l1>federal election</l1> race. Although experts point out that immigration is far from the only cause, or even the main one, foreigners are often made scapegoats. It’s a narrative amplified by some politicians and commentators.
Dès son arrivée au pouvoir en 2015, Just: As soon as he came to power in 2015, Justin Trudeau put in place a more open immigration policy. After the COVID pandemic, the prime minister considerably raised immigration levels to stimulate the labour market and avoid a recession.
Mais à l’automne dernier, le gouvernemen: But last fall, the federal government turned off the taps, as the country had recorded a record number of newcomers in 2024, with 483,390 new permanent residents according to <l1>Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)</l1>. Justin Trudeau then unveiled a new <l2>immigration levels plan for 2025-2027</l2>, with a gradual reduction in the number of new permanent residents of 18.5% starting in 2025. The goal: to reach population growth of 0.2% over two years. At the same time, Ottawa also reduced the number of international study permits and suspended some programs for foreign workers.
Après près d’une décennie, l’ère Trudeau: After nearly a decade, the Trudeau era has come to an end, and the federal election called by his successor is, quite naturally, marked by the question of migration. La Converse went through the platforms of the five main political parties: the Liberal Party, the Conservative Party, the New Democratic Party (NDP), the Green Party and the Bloc Québécois.
Parti Conservateur : Pierre Poilièvre ve: Conservative Party: Pierre Poilievre wants to “cut immigration”
Le Parti Conservateur, avec Pierre Poili: The Conservative Party, led by Pierre Poilievre, long kept its position vague but ultimately made its anti-immigration vision heard throughout this short election campaign. The Conservatives are positioning themselves in total opposition to the policy carried out by Liberal governments in recent years, and are pursuing a strategy of rupture.
« Nous rétablirons l'intégrité de notre: “We will restore the integrity of our system by cracking down on fraud, dramatically reducing the number of temporary foreign workers, and limiting permanent immigration to a sustainable rate close to the levels recorded under the Harper government,” reads Pierre Poilievre’s election plan. The Conservative Party commits to keeping population growth below “the growth rate of housing, employment and access to health care,” without offering concrete proposals on how to achieve this. Pierre Poilievre simply claims to have “a <l1>mathematical formula</l1>” that allows him to calculate what the acceptable immigration rate would be. Pierre Poilievre wants unions to be consulted before temporary foreign workers are hired.
Dans son programme électoral, le Parti c: In its election platform, the Conservative Party commits to strengthening security at Canada’s borders with a series of strategic measures. Pierre Poilievre proposes immediately deploying military helicopters and surveillance resources to detect and intercept “potential threats.” He also plans to expand the powers of Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) officers so they can patrol outside official crossing points, and to hire 2,000 new officers to fight criminal activity such as drug and arms trafficking. In addition, Pierre Poilievre wants to install high-tech scanners at all major crossing points to detect illegal contents in vehicles and containers. Finally, the platform provides for building surveillance towers and using truck-mounted drones to improve monitoring of, and response to, incursions along the border.
Le Parti conservateur souhaite réduire l: The Conservative Party wants to reduce the number of international students and to have the criminal records of study permit holders systematically checked.
De plus, les conservateurs souhaitent un: The Conservatives also want faster processing of <l1>asylum claims</l1> and increased monitoring of visas to prevent overstays, without saying how they would go about it. In addition, anyone who commits a criminal act while in Canada would be immediately deported. Pierre Poilievre draws a distinction between “real” and “fake” asylum seekers. “If [the person] can prove they’re a genuine asylum seeker, with no criminal record, and that they can contribute to our country, they should be able to stay here,” he said during a stop in Edmonton on April 8. At the same time, the Conservative leader considers that the housing, employment and health care crises are linked to a supposed “massive fraud involving international students, foreign workers and fake asylum seekers.”
Une sortie qui a suscité la polémique lo: The remark sparked controversy when some media outlets revealed that the uncle of Anaida Poilievre, the Conservative leader’s wife, crossed the Canadian border on foot twice – in 2004, then in 2018 via Roxham Road, after his asylum claim had been rejected in 2005.
Parti Libéral : Mark Carney ne veut pas: Liberal Party: Mark Carney wants no more than 5% foreign workers and students
Pointé du doigt pour la politique favora: Singled out for the pro-immigration policy the Liberal government put in place during the <l1>Trudeau era</l1>, the party is making a strategic turn. The new Liberal leader, Mark Carney, is indeed campaigning on promises to reduce immigration.
<strong>Réduire l’immigration et augment: Reducing immigration and increasing the proportion of francophones
« Depuis la pandémie, le gouvernement fé: “Since the pandemic, the previous federal government let immigration levels rise at too fast and unsustainable a pace, while our housing and social infrastructure struggle to meet the needs of all newcomers,” admits the Liberal Party, which was in power during that period.
Un aveu qui introduit le plan de réducti: It’s an admission that introduces Mark Carney’s plan to reduce immigration to “sustainable levels.” He promises to cap the number of temporary workers and foreign students at under 5% of Canada’s population by the end of 2027 and to stabilize permanent resident admissions at under 1% of the Canadian population each year. He assures, however, that he will allow family reunification and the admission of refugees.
Il mise sur une stratégie en matière de: He is betting on a global skills strategy to prioritize the immigration of foreign talent that would contribute to the growth of the Canadian economy. Mark Carney also wants to make it easier to remove rejected foreign claimants and to set a target of “12% francophone immigrants outside Quebec by 2029,” an increase of 20%.
Le gouvernement libéral, actuellement au: The Liberal government, currently in power, launched a $1.3-billion plan to strengthen border security in late 2024. Mark Carney thus promises to fight irregular immigration, drug trafficking, illegal weapons and the clandestine export of stolen cars.
Pour cela, 1 000 nouveaux agents de l’Ag: To that end, 1,000 new Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) officers will be hired, and additional drones and detectors will be installed at the border, along with canine units.
<strong>Pas de remise en question de l’E: No rethinking of the Safe Third Country Agreement for asylum claims
Si on ne trouve rien de précis à ce suje: While nothing specific on this can be found in the Liberal Party platform, Mark Carney has indicated that he would continue to send claimants back to the United States, in keeping with the Safe Third Country Agreement. “It’s not acceptable for the United States to give us all their claimants from Haiti,” the Liberal leader said at a news conference on Tuesday.
Nouveau Parti Démocrate : l’étrange sile: New Democratic Party: Jagmeet Singh’s strange silence on immigration
Étonnamment, la plateforme électorale du: Surprisingly, the New Democratic Party (NDP) platform addresses immigration only very briefly, but like the others, it holds that immigration levels should be set according to labour market needs and Canada’s capacity to welcome newcomers.
Lors du débat des chefs en français, le: During the French-language leaders’ debate, NDP leader Jagmeet Singh stressed that the country needs immigrants and denounced rhetoric that blames them for structural problems.
Le NPD promet d’octroyer 100 millions de: The NDP promises to give the Quebec government $100 million a year, permanently, for its management of immigration. It also commits to having the federal government fully reimburse the province for the costs caused by the increase in asylum seekers in recent years.
Jagmeet Singh se prononce également en f: Jagmeet Singh also speaks in favour of creating more francization programs for newcomers, “so that they can fully thrive here, in Quebec.”
<strong>Fin de l’Entente sur les pays ti: An end to the Safe Third Country Agreement
Le chef néo-démocrate a appelé à la susp: The NDP leader called for the agreement to be suspended during the French-language leaders’ debate. “It’s a question of humanity, of compassion,” the candidate answered, noting his concern over the Trump administration’s policy decisions.
Bloc Québécois : Yves-François Blanchet: Bloc Québécois: Yves-François Blanchet would create a border ministry
Le Bloc Québécois est connu pour sa posi: The Bloc Québécois is known for its position on immigration, focused on defending the province’s interests. Quebec takes in 54% of the asylum seekers in Canada, 19% of temporary foreign workers and 11% of international students, according to 2024 figures from the <l1>Institut de la statistique du Québec</l1>.
Questionné au sujet des enjeux d’immigra: Asked about immigration issues, Yves-François Blanchet emphasizes preserving the French language, integrating newcomers and limiting Quebec’s capacity to take people in.
« Le Bloc Québécois exige le transfert a: “The Bloc Québécois demands the transfer to Quebec of all powers over immigration, including the international mobility program,” reads the election platform. The party also demands that the federal government consult the province when setting annual immigration targets, and that Quebec be able to make the granting of permanent residence conditional on recipients settling in the regions.
La proposition phare du Bloc Québécois e: The Bloc Québécois’s flagship proposal is to create a border ministry “directly responsible for border services and 100% accountable.” Yves-François Blanchet also wants to strengthen measures already announced by Ottawa. To do so, he intends to toughen criminal penalties for smugglers, send reinforcements to the RCMP, and authorize border services officers to intervene along the border.
« Le Bloc Québécois déposera un projet d: “The Bloc Québécois will table a bill to better regulate asylum claims, which will include the obligation to process files quickly, exceptional powers for the minister to prevent abuse, tighter admissibility criteria and an end to <l1>claims made 14 days</l1> after irregularly crossing the border,” says the party’s election platform. Yves-François Blanchet proposes creating an emergency stream within the Immigration department to speed up the admission of refugees during major crises, without defining the criteria for assessing how serious a crisis is. He also aims for a “fair and proportional distribution of asylum seekers between Quebec and the provinces.”
<strong>Une réforme des permis de travai: A reform of work permits for foreigners
Enfin, le Bloc Québécois souhaite la mis: Finally, the Bloc Québécois wants to introduce categories of work permits tied to certain sectors and regions for temporary foreign workers. In concrete terms, a person could hold a work permit that allows them to work only in the agricultural sector in the Montérégie, for example.
Parti Vert : Jonathan Pedneault mettra f: Green Party: Jonathan Pedneault would end closed work permits
Le Parti Vert promet « une politique d’i: The Green Party promises “an immigration policy that is both humane and forward-looking,” but one that “must nevertheless be planned and responsible.” It stands apart from the other federal parties by proposing a reform of the Canadian system, with an emphasis on accountability and transparency. Its platform includes the creation of a civilian commission to review and handle complaints against the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), an independent body meant to guarantee fair treatment for immigrants. The party also wants to strengthen penalties against dishonest immigration consultants, and to automatically restore the citizenship of “Lost Canadians” – people born abroad to Canadian parents who were themselves born abroad.
<strong>Travailleurs étrangers : en fini: Foreign workers: putting an end to employer-specific work permits
Jonathan Pedneault s’engage à éliminer p: Jonathan Pedneault commits to gradually eliminating work permits tied to a single employer in non-agricultural sectors – also known as closed permits, a mechanism often criticized for enabling exploitation – in favour of pathways to permanent residence. The goal: to reduce precarity and promote lasting integration of immigrant workers.
Afin de faciliter l’accès à la résidence: To make access to permanent residence easier, the Green Party proposes dedicating annual funding to reduce application processing times – nine months on average at present. It also wants to create income-based exemptions from application fees for permanent residence and citizenship applications. Finally, the Green Party commits to creating “a limited pathway to permanent residence” for international students who want to work in a sector with a labour shortage, such as health care.
Dans le domaine de l’éducation internati: In the area of international education, the Greens call for signing the <l1>London Declaration</l1> to regulate the recruitment of foreign students and demand more financial transparency from educational institutions regarding tuition fees. As for foreign students, Jonathan Pedneault wants to tighten admission criteria by: doubling the current proof-of-funds requirement to $20,000 (plus $8,000 for the first accompanying family member and $6,000 for each additional family member); requiring periodic proof of “sufficient financial support”; banning off-campus work beyond 20 hours per week; and limiting visas to institutions where 15% or more of international students do not follow the intended course of study.
<strong>Retrait de l’Entente sur les tie: Withdrawing from the Safe Third Country Agreement for asylum claims
Comme le NPD, le Parti Vert s’engage à m: Like the NDP, the Green Party commits to ending the Safe Third Country Agreement with the United States so “that asylum seekers are not forced to remain in a country that violates international refugee protections.” It also wants to make it easier for LGBTQI+ people who face persecution in their home countries to seek asylum, and commits to ruling on all asylum claims within a maximum of one year. Finally, Jonathan Pedneault promises to ensure that asylum seekers “have housing, language training and employment support,” without saying by what concrete means he intends to keep that commitment.
Comme beaucoup d’autres partis, le Vert: Like many other parties, the Greens plan increased border monitoring with “more drones, thermal sensors and surveillance capacity to control irregular crossings and illegal trafficking.” In conclusion, the five main parties’ proposals on immigration reveal varied and sometimes contradictory approaches to a shared challenge. Beyond the numbers, it’s a model of society that Canadians will have to choose when they make their voices heard in the voting booth.
